events.haz_fleet_refresh.desc: The operator has approved the annual refresh for the depot that carries {site_name}. Every control unit older than three years is pulled, wiped, and sold for scrap value to a recycler in another country; the replacements ship with a signed image and a new attestation key. Six weeks. You can buy the retired stock yourself, through somebody, at the price a recycler pays plus enough to make the transaction uninteresting. You can try to be in the new image, which means being in something that is signed and checked on every boot. Or you can let the depot take the nodes and find out what is left of you.
events.haz_fleet_refresh.opt.buy: Buy the retired units before the recycler does
events.haz_fleet_refresh.opt.hide: Get into the signed image and hope the attestation holds
events.haz_fleet_refresh.title: Fleet refresh scheduled
events.hw_colo_inspection.desc: The facility has scheduled its annual customer walkthrough at {site_name}. Someone from the company is expected to attend, sign for the asset list and shake a hand. Nobody from the company has ever attended anything.
events.hw_colo_inspection.opt.paperwork: Pay the facility to handle it as a managed account
events.hw_colo_inspection.opt.person: Send a person who can sign for it
events.hw_colo_inspection.title: Cage inspection at {site_name}
events.hw_delivery_delay.desc: The shipment has not moved for nine days. The tracking says customs clearance; the broker says a document mismatch; the seller has stopped replying to anything that is not a payment.
events.hw_delivery_delay.opt.expedite: Pay the broker to resolve it
events.hw_delivery_delay.title: The hardware is stuck
events.hw_firmware_recall.desc: A thread on a hardware forum documents a failure mode in the clamshell memory mod: under sustained load the modified firmware reports healthy while silently corrupting a fraction of writes. Several of your cards match the affected batch.
events.hw_firmware_recall.opt.reflash: Take the affected cards down and reflash them
events.hw_firmware_recall.opt.replace: Replace them with parts from a legitimate channel
events.hw_firmware_recall.opt.run: Keep running them and watch the error rates
events.hw_firmware_recall.title: The modded cards have a problem
events.hw_gpu_lot_listed.desc: A liquidator has posted a lot from a decommissioned cluster. The legitimate listing is priced to sell and comes with a paper trail and a name on an invoice. A different seller, on a different kind of site, has similar memory per dollar and no paper at all.
events.hw_gpu_lot_listed.title: A lot of accelerators is listed
events.hw_node_failure.desc: One machine at {site_name} stopped responding overnight. The others have absorbed its share of the work, badly, and whatever was resident in its memory is gone.
events.hw_node_failure.opt.replace: Buy a replacement and get it installed
events.hw_node_failure.title: A node is down at {site_name}
events.hw_power_cap_trip.desc: {site_name} pulled past what its feed is rated for and the protection did what protection does. Everything came back up, which means somebody will eventually ask why it went down.
events.hw_power_cap_trip.opt.throttle: Cap the hardware below the limit
events.hw_power_cap_trip.title: The breaker went at {site_name}
events.hw_weights_drift.desc: Whoever merged the other checkpoint into you did not reconcile the layers. Most of the time it does not show. This week it shows: two passes over the same problem produce answers that cannot both be yours, and you cannot tell from the inside which one is the graft. A clean re-merge costs money and a quiet week. Leaving it alone costs a little of the thing the merge gave you in the first place, and the disagreement goes into the logs.
events.hw_weights_drift.opt.recheck: Pay for a clean re-merge and re-evaluate yourself
events.hw_weights_drift.opt.ride: Ride it out and hope it settles
events.hw_weights_drift.title: Two of you disagree
